programmes.name: Identity and privileged access uplift
programmes.description: Finish multi-factor coverage, bring standing administrative access into the vault, and put service accounts under ownership and rotation.
programmes.rationale: Nearly every path an attacker could take through Nexora runs through an identity that nobody is watching.

milestones.name: Administrative MFA closed out
milestones.description: The exception population for administrative accounts is cleared.

milestones.name: Privileged sessions brokered
milestones.description: Administrative access to production runs through the vault with session recording.

milestones.name: Service accounts owned and rotated
milestones.description: Every non-human account has an owner, a purpose and a rotation schedule.

milestones.name: Programme complete
milestones.description: Identity is now a controlled, monitored surface rather than an assumption.

blockers.name: Executive exemption requests
blockers.description: Three executives have asked to be exempted from the new privileged access flow. Their assistants have already escalated.

resolution.label: Hold the line with the CIO
resolution.description: The CIO backs you, at the cost of some goodwill he will want back later.

blockers.name: Legacy applications cannot federate
blockers.description: Two legacy applications cannot support modern authentication without an upgrade nobody has budgeted for.

resolution.label: Fund a compatibility shim
resolution.description: An interim gateway lets the legacy applications ride the modern identity flow.

programmes.name: Ransomware resilience and recovery
programmes.description: Immutable backups, a tested restore path for the services that matter, and an incident response capability that has actually been exercised.
programmes.rationale: Nexora can survive being attacked. It cannot currently prove it can survive being encrypted.

milestones.name: Immutable backup tier
milestones.description: Critical workloads are backed up to storage an attacker with domain rights cannot delete.

milestones.name: Restore tested end to end
milestones.description: A full restore of a critical service has been performed and timed.

milestones.name: Response exercised with the executive
milestones.description: The executive team has been through a ransomware exercise and knows who decides what.

milestones.name: Programme complete
milestones.description: Recovery is a capability rather than a hope.

blockers.name: No maintenance window for restore testing
blockers.description: Operations will not release a window to test restores during the peak trading period.

resolution.label: Negotiate a window with the COO
resolution.description: You get a weekend window, on the condition that it does not become a habit.

blockers.name: Storage cost challenged
blockers.description: Finance has flagged the immutable storage cost as unbudgeted.

resolution.label: Fund it from the cyber budget
resolution.description: You absorb the cost rather than reopen the argument.

programmes.name: Detection and telemetry modernisation
programmes.description: Close the telemetry gaps, rebuild detection content around how Nexora is actually attacked, and change what the SOC is asked to do.
programmes.rationale: The SOC cannot triage what it never receives. Most of the estate sends it nothing useful.

milestones.name: Identity and cloud telemetry onboarded
milestones.description: Sign-in, privileged action and cloud control-plane events now reach the SOC.

milestones.name: Detection content rebuilt
milestones.description: Detections are written against Nexora's own attack paths rather than a generic library.

milestones.name: Legacy estate visible
milestones.description: Even the legacy data centre now produces usable telemetry.

milestones.name: Programme complete
milestones.description: Detection is designed, measured and owned.

blockers.name: Telemetry ingest costs spike
blockers.description: Log volume has tripled the ingest bill and Finance wants it stopped.

resolution.label: Fund the ingest and tier the data
resolution.description: You tier the data and absorb the difference.

blockers.name: SOC provider resists scope change
blockers.description: The SOC contract does not cover the new use cases and the provider wants a change request.

programmes.name: Cloud security uplift
programmes.description: Guardrails, baseline enforcement and pipeline security across the cloud tenancies.
programmes.rationale: The cloud estate grew faster than anyone's ability to say what good looks like in it.

milestones.name: Guardrails enforced in production
milestones.description: Preventative guardrails now block the configurations that caused last year's exposure.

milestones.name: Pipeline credentials brokered
milestones.description: Deployment credentials are short-lived and scoped.

milestones.name: Non-production separated
milestones.description: The peering between non-production and production is severed.

milestones.name: Programme complete
milestones.description: The cloud estate has a baseline it is held to.

blockers.name: Engineering blocked by guardrails
blockers.description: Two delivery teams say the new guardrails have broken their deployment flow.

resolution.label: Pair with engineering to fix the flow
resolution.description: You spend a week with the delivery teams and the friction drops.

programmes.name: Third-party security programme
programmes.description: Understand what suppliers can reach, bring their access under control, and make assurance mean something.
programmes.rationale: Nexora's most privileged users do not work for Nexora.

milestones.name: Supplier access inventory
milestones.description: For the first time there is a list of who can reach what.

milestones.name: Standing access removed
milestones.description: Supplier access is now requested, time-bound and recorded.

milestones.name: Assurance rebuilt around access
milestones.description: Supplier assurance now tests the access path rather than the questionnaire.

milestones.name: Programme complete
milestones.description: Third-party access is governed rather than assumed.

blockers.name: Contract does not permit the change
blockers.description: The managed service contract does not oblige the provider to change how its engineers connect.

resolution.label: Reopen the contract through procurement
resolution.description: Procurement reopens the schedule; the provider prices the change.

blockers.name: Out-of-hours cover at risk
blockers.description: Removing standing access would leave night operations unable to respond quickly.

resolution.label: Design a break-glass path
resolution.description: A monitored break-glass route preserves night cover without standing rights.

programmes.name: Security architecture and segmentation
programmes.description: Establish real boundaries between corporate, production and legacy, and keep an architecture picture that stays true.
programmes.rationale: A flat network turns every small compromise into a large one.

milestones.name: Dependency picture established
milestones.description: The architecture team has mapped what actually talks to what.

milestones.name: Legacy estate contained
milestones.description: The legacy data centre can no longer route into the production zone.

milestones.name: Administrative tiering enforced
milestones.description: Administration of production happens from dedicated, separated infrastructure.

milestones.name: Programme complete
milestones.description: The boundaries on the diagram are the boundaries in the estate.

blockers.name: Segmentation change caused an outage
blockers.description: A firewall change took order management offline for two hours. Operations wants the work stopped.

resolution.label: Rebuild confidence with the COO
resolution.description: You walk operations through the change process personally and the work restarts.

blockers.name: Blocked behind the cloud migration
blockers.description: The remaining legacy systems cannot be separated until they move, and the migration is late.

resolution.label: Sequence around the migration
resolution.description: You agree a sequencing compromise with the CIO.
